column1: # What enforces each requirement in this library's specs (0024-spec-format FR-011 - FR-014).
# mechanism: check | gate | review | none. by: "<repo>: <command>" for check and gate, the defining requirement for review, "-" for none.

column4: note
suite/governance-neutral.test.ts: the code of governance names no engine and no part of a relational schema; its imports are held by FR-004 (engine and kernel only)

suite/logical-project.test.ts: a logical schema is made from governance by a projection; suite/logical-neutral.test.ts: it names no engine; its imports (governance, the engine and the kernel) are held by FR-004

suite/physical-bind.test.ts and suite/physical-engines.test.ts: a physical schema is made from a logical schema, a dialect and a naming; suite/physical-neutral.test.ts: only the dialects know an engine; its imports are held by FR-004
suite/layers.test.ts: each unit may import only the units of the table, and an import that climbs or reaches around is layers/above or layers/around, by package name and by path
suite/layers.test.ts: layers 1 to 3 and the engine import only the kernel and the library, and a driver or node:fs is layers/external

suite/logical-project.test.ts: every logical element carries the identity of its governance element (from); suite/physical-bind.test.ts: every statement carries the logical elements it was made from (of)
suite/documentation.test.ts: every annotation is a row of governance_annotation (carried) or a comment (expressed), and the logical flow report names what is unexpressed
suite/layers.test.ts: every file of the real tree is in a unit, and one in no unit is layers/unclassified
suite/layers.test.ts: the four layer entries of exports are the api.ts of their folders, and an import of a subpath exports does not name is layers/private
suite/layers.test.ts: a relative import into another unit is layers/relative, and one inside the unit is not
suite/layers.test.ts: the check finds nothing in the real tree, each rule is found in a copy, and verify runs tools/check.ts
suite/layers.test.ts: the engine imports nothing of the library, and only the kernel by package name
suite/engine.test.ts: a point carries its name and is frozen, and a name with no namespace does not compile
suite/engine-manifest.test.ts: an identifier is checked, a manifest is frozen data with the engine's contract and empty lists by default, and a lazy entry holds what is known before it loads
suite/engine-manifest.test.ts: a contribution is typed by its point, and a value of another type does not compile (@ts-expect-error, checked by the compiler in verify)
suite/engine-compose.test.ts: an extension defined in an imported module is in no composition until the project lists it, and a second composition shares nothing with the first

suite/engine-compose.test.ts: the order satisfies requires and keeps the project's order, and a duplicate, a missing extension, a cycle, a contract the engine lacks and a handle not provided come back together as values
suite/engine-compose.test.ts: the contributions of a point come back typed and in the order of the composition

suite/engine-activation.test.ts: start activates in order once, a lazy extension loads and activates once on its event (two at once too) after what it requires, and a bad load, a failed load and a throwing activate are values that stay
suite/engine-activation.test.ts: use gives only a declared and provided handle, typed by it; undeclared and unprovided are error values, for a lazy extension too
suite/governance-model.test.ts: the constructors are total and the pieces are frozen data with their defaults; a domain is the domain when nothing is wrong
suite/governance-model.test.ts: every case of the datatype union is described, and none names a database
suite/governance-model.test.ts: the names of a concept are literal types, and an identifying attribute or relationship it lacks does not compile (@ts-expect-error, checked in verify)

suite/governance-model.test.ts: a bad name (not lower camel case), a duplicate, an annotation out of place, an unresolved relationship or code list, and a bad identifier (none, optional, a relationship that is not one, unknown) come back together as values; a relationship given as a function allows a cycle
suite/governance-elements.test.ts: an identity is made of names, and every element is listed in a fixed order with its kind, name, definition and parent
suite/governance-elements.test.ts: the trace graph has the elements as nodes and contains, identifies (an attribute or a relationship) and references as edges, each joining two nodes
suite/governance-annotations.test.ts: an annotation is typed by its kind, says where it may be, and is read back typed (@ts-expect-error, checked in verify)
suite/governance-annotations.test.ts: an extension contributes a vocabulary through the engine and the composition gives them in order
suite/governance-annotations.test.ts: lint returns data, the core rules first (a missing definition, an unknown kind) and then each vocabulary's in order
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: the documentation kinds go where they say and the vocabulary has no rule
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: a citation is NNNN-slug FR-nnn, requirementsOf says who cites what, and the uncited and malformed rules fire and stay quiet
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: personal data names a DPV-PD term (a term that is not one does not compile), dpvClassOf and dpvIri, and the category and purpose rules

suite/governance-dpv.test.ts: a CSV that is not the pinned one is refused and the generated file carries the pinned source and digest; the live --check against the CSV runs in .github/workflows/data.yml
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: the security kinds go where they say, and the scope, restricted-access and personal-unprotected rules fire and stay quiet
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: owner and steward go on a domain, a concept or a code list, and the owner-missing rule fires and stays quiet

suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: the quality kinds (pattern, range, retention, deprecated, default, unique, differs, audited, openness) go where they say, and each rule fires and stays quiet, a default being held to its datatype
suite/governance-vocabularies.test.ts: a lookup goes on a concept and says its members, and one that names a member the concept lacks is found
suite/arca.test.ts: the party model is a valid domain named arca_party given as a result; its imports (governance only) are held by 0001-layers FR-004

suite/arca.test.ts: the concepts, code lists, attributes and relationships are those of the model it replaces, and every old table and column is accounted for by the domain and the conventions a layer below must follow
suite/arca.test.ts: a person and an organization are identified by their relationship of cardinality one to a party, every other concept by an attribute named for it
suite/arca.test.ts: every element has a definition and lint with every vocabulary of the library finds nothing
suite/arca.test.ts: each personal attribute names an existing DPV-PD category and a purpose, and every concept that holds personal data is confidential
suite/arca.test.ts: the four reference code lists carry the codes, labels and definitions of the old reference data and are open; the two closed lists carry theirs
suite/arca.test.ts: the domain is audited with removal by marking, and has an owner
suite/arca.test.ts: one identifier of a kind, parties_differ, the default of is_primary and each lookup are said as governance
suite/arca.test.ts: every concept cites requirements and every citation names a requirement that exists in this library's specifications
suite/naming.test.ts: a name is lower camel case, and domain returns a name with an underscore or a capital first as an error, for every kind of element
suite/naming.test.ts: words splits at lower to upper, around digits and at the end of a run of capitals; for 500 generated names the words are at least one, stable, and join back to the name
suite/logical-project.test.ts: the words of tables, columns, foreign keys, uniques, checks and indexes follow the conventions, and reproduce the old model's names in snake case
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: a list of words is written in the case style with the dialect's quoting and length limit
suite/physical-case.test.ts: a case style is added by an extension through physical.caseStyle, and snake case is the default
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: codes are written by the style (employed_by), by another style, or as their names; suite/physical-engines.test.ts: the reference rows hold employed_by
suite/logical-project.test.ts: two elements named alike once made are returned with the elements that clash
Planned: governance's names and words are built (0005-naming FR-001, FR-002); the logical and physical conventions come with those layers
suite/arca.test.ts: every name is lower camel case, and the words of the domain's names make the old model's tables and columns in snake case
suite/logical-project.test.ts: the schema is plain data whose tables, columns, constraints and value sets have identities of their own and a `from`
suite/logical-project.test.ts: the logical type of every datatype, none an engine's
suite/logical-project.test.ts: project returns the schema as a value or every error, a projection given to it, and one contributed through the engine's logical.projection
suite/logical-project.test.ts: a concept is a table, an open code list a code table with its rows, a closed one a value set and no table

suite/logical-project.test.ts: every old table's columns come from the words of the attributes and relationships, the key first; many relationships and attributes, optional relationships and a key of several columns on small domains; a cycle of identities is an error value

suite/logical-project.test.ts: the constraints and indexes have the names the old model's SQLite golden gave them (14 and 6); defaults, ranges and patterns are made; a member that is not there is an error value
suite/logical-project.test.ts: audit columns on every concept table and none on a code table, removal by deleting leaves out the removal columns, and the moment of the insert is the default
suite/logical-project.test.ts: the comment of a table and of a column is the definition of what it was made from
suite/logical-project.test.ts: two tables, two columns and two constraints named alike are returned with the elements that clash

suite/logical-project.test.ts: every element's from is an element of the domain, and a table, a column, a foreign key column and a code table are traced to their concept, attribute, relationship and list

suite/logical-flow.test.ts: every annotation is in the report once; expressed ones name the constraints and columns they became, carried ones the elements that keep them; an unknown kind is unexpressed, and carried where told
suite/logical-rows.test.ts: RowOf, InsertOf and KeyOf are computed from a concept and the compiler holds them (@ts-expect-error, checked in verify)
suite/logical-neutral.test.ts: the code of the logical schema names no engine and no type of one
suite/physical-case.test.ts: snake, camel and pascal write words as names, the words of a valid name written in camel are that name (500 generated), and an extension adds a style through the engine
suite/physical-case.test.ts: writeCode by style, by another style or as the name; suite/physical-bind.test.ts: the codes of reference rows and closed-list checks follow it
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: a name too long for PostgreSQL and names that are alike once written are error values with the elements that clash
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: the DDL of a small domain written out for each dialect, the three as extensions through physical.dialect, and each dialect's quoting, literals and features
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: a pattern is a check on PostgreSQL and DuckDB and an error value naming the check on SQLite
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: tables follow the tables they refer to, indexes follow tables, data follows both, a cycle is added afterwards or is an error value
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with typed columns, NOT NULL, defaults, inline or composite primary keys and named constraints; CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: reference rows are upserts with the codes written by style; suite/physical-engines.test.ts: loaded twice they leave the same rows, on each engine
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: every statement carries the logical elements it was made from, each in the schema
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: the same input gives the same text, and statements an extension adds are kept apart by group, in order
suite/physical-bind.test.ts: an extension adds statements through physical.statements, is given the written names, and its errors are returned with bind's

suite/physical-engines.test.ts: on SQLite, DuckDB and PostgreSQL (PGlite) the engine holds the logical schema's tables, columns, nullability, primary keys and indexes, refuses what its constraints forbid, and keeps the reference data stable
suite/physical-neutral.test.ts: the code of the physical core names no engine, and each dialect names its own and no other
suite/documentation.test.ts: the comments extension writes COMMENT ON for each table and column where the dialect has it, quotes doubled
suite/documentation.test.ts: the documentation table holds one row per described table and column, and only where the settings ask for it
suite/documentation.test.ts: the governance tables hold the annotations and the trace of each written column
suite/documentation.test.ts: a comment holds the human description alone
suite/documentation.test.ts: the settings are a typed value with the defaults the spec gives
suite/documentation.test.ts: each extension contributes a statement source to physical.statements and can be left out
suite/documentation.test.ts: the extension tables are bound by the physical schema's own machinery, a name collision is an error value
suite/documentation.test.ts: loading twice leaves the same rows, and reloading after a change leaves the new ones
suite/documentation.test.ts: every annotation of the domain is a row of governance_annotation, an unknown kind included
suite/features.test.ts: the groups run setup first, then tables, then what features add, and policy last
suite/features.test.ts: the dialects name the features they have, and an extension asks for the feature
suite/features.test.ts: a dialect refuses a type with a reason, and runs setup statements for the types a schema uses
suite/features.test.ts: an extension adds a clause to a table through physical.tableClauses
suite/features.test.ts: a view is made from a typed definition by governance names and returns the rows its conditions give on three engines
suite/features.test.ts: a view is replaced or dropped and made again by the dialect, with its description as a comment where there is one
suite/features.test.ts: a view that names what the schema lacks is an error value, and its statement carries what it reads
suite/features.test.ts: a scoped table shows a role only the rows of its scope on PostgreSQL, and applying twice leaves the same policies
suite/features.test.ts: grants follow the roles of security.access and a policy is made for each role's operations
suite/features.test.ts: where the dialect lacks the feature nothing is written, or an error value where the setting says
suite/features.test.ts: a routine is made by CREATE OR REPLACE on PostgreSQL and an error value elsewhere
suite/features.test.ts: a body of text and typed references is written with the names of the case style, and a bad reference is an error value
suite/features.test.ts: a routine's description is its comment with the parameter types
suite/features.test.ts: a partitioned table keeps each row in the partition of its bounds, by range, list and hash
suite/features.test.ts: a division whose key is not a column or not in the primary key, or whose dialect cannot partition, is an error value
suite/features.test.ts: a vector is VECTOR(n) after the extension on PostgreSQL, FLOAT[n] on DuckDB and refused on SQLite
suite/features.test.ts: a vector of fewer than one dimension, or not a whole number, is an error value from domain()
suite/features.test.ts: each feature does what it says on a real engine
suite/generators.test.ts: extensions contribute generators through the engine, and generate returns every file in order or every error
suite/generators.test.ts: the same input gives the same files, each ending in one newline, and the generators read nothing but what they are given
suite/generators.test.ts: the path is made from the domain, and a path made twice is an error value
suite/generators.test.ts: names are written by the case style, and no generator reads anything but its input
suite/generators.test.ts: the Mermaid and D2 diagrams hold every table, type, key mark and foreign key, and a closed list is an enum
suite/generators.test.ts: the dictionary holds each table's description, owner, key and columns with type, null, target, description and personal data
suite/generators.test.ts: the page has the dictionary with links, no script and no outside resource
suite/generators.test.ts: Rust has a struct with Options and an enum for a closed list
suite/generators.test.ts: Zod has a schema with nullable and z.enum
suite/generators.test.ts: the register lists personal data and security
suite/generators.test.ts: every logical type has a form in Rust and Zod
suite/generators.test.ts: a text of governance is escaped for Markdown, HTML and documentation comments
suite/generators.test.ts: the Zod module validates rows and refuses what does not fit, and the Rust file compiles
suite/generators.test.ts: the files of Arca's party model hold every table, column and foreign key of the schema and nothing more
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: the lifecycle is a unit with a public surface, and its files name no engine
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: a state is a hashed value, the same for the same structure in any order, and the hash is the kernel's SHA-256
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: bind marks what it makes as the core's and what an extension adds as the extension's
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: tables and columns are matched by their words, so a change of case style is a rename, and renamedFrom makes a rename
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: the changes of any two states lead from the first to the second (property test)
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: changes are classified by what they could lose and whether they can be undone
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: a plan has the ordered steps with the state hashes each needs and leaves, content identifiers, and none between equal states
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: destructive steps are refused unless allowed, what the dialect cannot do needs a person's step, and all errors are returned together
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: what extensions add is repeatable with a key and a hash, and only what changed is due
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: a ledger whose entry was changed, taken out, put in or moved fails its chain
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: a plan runs on three real engines step by step with the ledger, does nothing run again, refuses another base, rolls back a failed step and finds a touched ledger
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: the plans from empty and from each version to the next leave the database bind makes for the last version, on three engines
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: for any two states applying the diff reaches the second, and the diff of a state with itself is empty (property test)
suite/lifecycle.test.ts: the lifecycle vocabulary exists and lint finds a renamedFrom that is not a name or is the element's own
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a dialect says which forms have IF EXISTS and gives probes that find a table, column, constraint and index on the engine
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a run skips a guarded statement whose work is done, and the guard is part of the identity of the step
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a statement is natural where the dialect has a form, guarded where it has none, and idempotent statements are left as they are
suite/idempotency.test.ts: each step says whether it is natural, guarded or ledger-only, for the statements that do it and that undo it
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a step a person wrote relies on the ledger unless it is guarded
suite/idempotency.test.ts: the transform is an extension that contributes through lifecycle.transform, is in the default composition, and can be left out or switched off
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a project can refuse a step that only the ledger keeps from running twice
suite/idempotency.test.ts: a guarded statement is one DO block on PostgreSQL that does no harm run twice, and is refused where the dialect has no block
suite/idempotency.test.ts: on three real engines every step and every plan can be run twice without the ledger with the result of running it once
